question: Plainer version of q16. Three things get counted in each agent's home: how often each note is looked up, how many friction entries pile up, and how often each rule fires. Per agent, as you said. The only open choice is storage. (A) One small file per home, say metrics.json, holding all three counts, updated by one shared script. (B) Each count stored where it arises: note counts inside the notes folder, friction counts derived from the history log on demand, rule firings in the router's firing log filtered by agent. A is one place to read and one writer to get right; B adds no new file but means three ways of reading. Which?

Follow-up to q17. 'Private repos for the skills' can mean two layouts. (A) One repository covering the host's skill folder: simplest, and worktrees stay as the spec describes. (B) One repository per skill: each skill versions on its own, a worktree then holds only that skill, which also removes the .claude/skills segment from copy paths, and the global option can push each skill to its own remote. And does private mean a local repository only, or a private remote on GitHub created with gh?
